name: SFR Directory Analytics
author: SupportFromRichard

sections.description:
SFR Directory Analytics provides comprehensive analytics tracking for popular WordPress directory plugins. Understanding which listings attract visitors helps you optimise content, improve user experience, and make data-driven decisions for your directory website.

Track page views for individual listings and categories with beautiful, easy-to-understand dashboards that reveal exactly what your visitors are interested in.

Supported Directory Plugins

  • Directorist – Track listings and categories
  • GeoDirectory – Monitor place views and category performance
  • Business Directory Plugin – Analyse listing and category engagement

Key Features

  • Beautiful Analytics Dashboard – View your data with colourful charts and graphs
  • Real-Time Tracking – Automatic view tracking for listings and categories
  • Time Period Analysis – See views for Today, Last 7 Days, Last 30 Days, and All Time
  • Visual Charts – Daily, weekly (12 weeks), and monthly (12 months) trend charts
  • Top Performers – Identify your most viewed listings and categories
  • Privacy-Focused – All data stored locally in your WordPress database
  • Multi-Site Ready – Each website installation tracks independently
  • Lightweight – Minimal performance impact with efficient database writes
  • Cache-Friendly – Compatible with popular caching plugins

Perfect For

  • Directory website owners wanting to understand visitor behaviour
  • Businesses tracking which listings get the most attention
  • Website developers optimising directory performance
  • Content creators identifying popular categories
  • Marketing teams measuring campaign effectiveness
  • Site owners preparing for directory monetisation

How It Works

  1. Install and activate SFR Directory Analytics
  2. The plugin automatically detects your directory plugin
  3. Views are tracked automatically when visitors view listings or categories
  4. View beautiful analytics in WordPress Admin > Directory Analytics

No configuration required – it works right out of the box!

Privacy & Data

  • All analytics data stored locally in your WordPress database
  • No external API calls or data sharing
  • GDPR compliant – no personal information collected
  • Does not require cookie consent (only tracks page views, not user behaviour)
  • Can exclude administrator views from tracking
  • Configurable data retention (7-365 days)
  • Minimal database footprint – efficient storage design

Technical Details

  • Database Impact: Uses WordPress options table – no custom tables created
  • Performance: Efficient tracking with no impact on page load times
  • Caching: Fully compatible with WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, and other popular caching plugins
  • Tracking Method: Page view counts only (not unique visitors)
  • Data Storage: Approximately 1KB per 100 views tracked
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin files to /wp-content/plugins/sfr-directory-analytics/, or install through WordPress plugins screen
  2. Activate the plugin through the ‘Plugins’ screen in WordPress
  3. Ensure you have Directorist, GeoDirectory, or Business Directory Plugin active
  4. Go to Directory Analytics in admin menu to view your dashboard
  5. Configure settings under Directory Analytics > Settings if needed

That’s it! The plugin will automatically start tracking views.
sections.faq:
Which directory plugins are supported?

Currently supports Directorist, GeoDirectory, and Business Directory Plugin. More integrations coming soon.

Does this work with multiple directory plugins at once?

Yes! If you have multiple directory plugins active, SFR Directory Analytics will track all of them simultaneously.

Will this slow down my website?

No. Tracking is lightweight and uses WordPress best practices. Data is written efficiently to your database with minimal overhead. The plugin is designed to have zero impact on page load times.

Does this track unique visitors or just page views?

The plugin tracks total page views, not unique visitors. This means if the same person views a listing multiple times, each view is counted.

Why are my category view counts higher than listing view counts?

This is normal and by design! Category views represent total engagement across all listings in that category. When a visitor views a listing, each of its assigned top-level categories also receives a view count. For example, if a listing is in 3 categories and gets 100 views, those 3 categories will each receive 100 views, resulting in 300 total category views. This helps you understand which categories drive the most overall engagement across your directory.

Can I see which traffic sources bring views to my listings?

Not in the current version. Traffic source tracking is planned for a future update.

Can I exclude my own views from analytics?

Yes! Go to Directory Analytics > Settings and enable “Exclude Administrators” to exclude admin views from being tracked.

How long is data retained?

By default, 90 days of historical data is kept. You can configure this from 7-365 days in the Settings page.

Is this GDPR compliant?

Yes. All data is stored locally in your WordPress database. No personal information is collected – only view counts for pages. The plugin does not track individual users or require cookie consent.

Does this affect my website’s GDPR cookie requirements?

No. Since the plugin only counts page views and doesn’t track individual users or set cookies, it doesn’t affect your cookie consent requirements.

Does each website track separately?

Yes. Each WordPress installation maintains its own independent analytics database. Perfect for using the same plugin across multiple client sites.

What happens if I deactivate one of my directory plugins?

The analytics data for that plugin is preserved in the database. If you reactivate the directory plugin later, historical data will still be available.

Does this work with caching plugins?

Yes! SFR Directory Analytics is fully compatible with popular caching plugins including WP Rocket, W3 Total Cache, WP Super Cache, and others.

Can I export the analytics data?

Export functionality (CSV/PDF) will be available in a future update.

How much database space does this use?

Very minimal. The plugin uses approximately 1KB per 100 views tracked. Even high-traffic sites will see negligible database growth.
sections.changelog:
1.0.4

  • Feature: Added the Support From Richard Toolkit panel so site owners can discover other free SFR plugins, launch their dashboards, and jump to the Support From Richard tools directory.
  • Enhancement: Added a “Refresh Integrations” option (and automatic cache clears on activation/deactivation) so switching between Directorist, Business Directory, or GeoDirectory updates analytics immediately without waiting for a transient to expire.
  • Enhancement: Improved the Directory Map companion card with clearer upgrade context and consistent CTA placement.
  • Fix: Removed the manual load_plugin_textdomain() call; WordPress now loads translations automatically, eliminating Plugin Check warnings.
  • Fix: Prefixed all template-level variables to pass the latest WordPress.org coding standards checks.

1.0.3

  • Improved: Added clear explanation of how category view tracking works
  • Added: Info box on dashboard explaining category engagement methodology
  • Added: FAQ entry explaining why category views can be higher than listing views
  • Documentation: Clarified that categories receive views when their associated listings are viewed
  • Note: No code changes – purely documentation improvements for user clarity

1.0.2

  • Fixed: Moved all inline scripts and styles to proper WordPress enqueue functions
  • Changed: JavaScript now loaded via wp_add_inline_script() for WordPress.org compliance
  • Changed: CSS animations now loaded via wp_add_inline_style() for WordPress.org compliance
  • Improved: Better compliance with WordPress.org plugin review standards
  • Note: No functional changes – purely technical improvements for code quality

1.0.1

  • Improved: Category tracking methodology completely rebuilt for better reliability
  • Changed: Categories now tracked based on listing category assignments rather than URL structure
  • Enhanced: Tracks only top-level parent categories (sub-categories excluded for cleaner data)
  • Removed: URL-based category detection eliminated (locations and tags no longer tracked)
  • How it works now: Categories accumulate views whenever any listing assigned to that category is viewed
  • Why this change: URL-based tracking was unreliable across different directory setups and permalink structures
  • Migration note: No action required – historical listing data is preserved, category data will rebuild naturally
  • Result: More accurate category analytics that reflect actual listing engagement

1.0.0

  • Initial release
  • Support for Directorist, GeoDirectory, and Business Directory Plugin
  • Listing view tracking
  • Category view tracking
  • Beautiful analytics dashboard
  • Daily, weekly, and monthly charts
  • Top performers lists
  • Configurable settings
  • Data retention management
  • Admin view exclusion option
